search_bias: evaluation/verifiers; measurement-validity/benchmark-design; few-independent-unit sequential inference, paired/stratified anytime-validity, and dependence-aware stopping

sources_checked_or_revisited.title: Safe Sequential Testing and Effect Estimation in Stratified Count Data
sources_checked_or_revisited.authors: Rosanne J. Turner, Peter D. Grunwald
sources_checked_or_revisited.action: Extracted exact e-process/confidence-sequence construction for stratified 2x2 count streams, block-level optional stopping, adaptive past-determined block sizes, and cross-talk power tradeoffs.

sources_checked_or_revisited.title: Martingale Methods for Sequential Estimation of Convex Functionals and Divergences
sources_checked_or_revisited.action: Extracted paired-sample time-uniform two-sample bounds that permit within-pair dependence and are tighter than generic two-stream bounds, plus stopping-time/filtration scope.

sources_checked_or_revisited.title: Near-Optimal Non-Parametric Sequential Tests and Confidence Sequences with Possibly Dependent Observations
sources_checked_or_revisited.authors: Aurelien Bibaut, Nathan Kallus, Michael Lindon
sources_checked_or_revisited.action: Extracted delayed-start uSPRT/nmSPRT guarantees under possibly dependent nonparametric observations, burn-in calibration, finite simulation protocol, and exact-vs-asymptotic validity boundary.

sources_checked_or_revisited.title: Design-Based Confidence Sequences: A General Approach to Risk Mitigation in Online Experimentation
sources_checked_or_revisited.authors: Dae Woong Ham, Iavor Bojinov, Michael Lindon, Martin Tingley
sources_checked_or_revisited.action: Extracted design-based time-uniform inference for randomized sequential experiments, finite-study-participant estimands, panel/time-series support, and the Netflix early-stop example.

sources_checked_or_revisited.title: Group sequential methods for cluster randomization trials with binary outcomes
sources_checked_or_revisited.authors: Guang Yong Zou, Allan Donner, Neil Klar
sources_checked_or_revisited.action: Revisited finite-cluster binary group-sequential evidence: four of five statistics reportedly satisfactory with 10 clusters per intervention under the tested CRT design, with asymptotic independent-increment structure.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: For binary/paired agent outcomes that can be organized into completed independent task blocks or prespecified strata, use block-level e-variables and multiply them into an e-process. Let block composition/sample size depend only on past completed blocks, and permit optional stopping only on completed blocks. If heterogeneity structure is useful, combine stratum-specific e-processes through past-determined pseudo-Bayesian weighting/switching rather than pooling all records as iid.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Turner and Grunwald construct exact e-processes for stratified 2x2 streams. Their setup treats each arriving block as one stratum-specific batch and permits n_a,n_b to be chosen adaptively between blocks from the past. Ville-type control gives optional-stopping validity. In simulations, 40 batches were collected in each of three strata (maximum m=120) across 1000 repeated experiments; all stratification-aware combination methods outperformed the unstratified approach in the heterogeneous setting. The paper also constructs exact anytime-valid risk-difference confidence sequences and allows past-determined cross-talk between strata, with simulations showing narrower intervals when the borrowed structure matches and worse behavior when strata truly differ.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope: Exact under the paper's block model: completed blocks are independent, and outcomes within each group/stratum block follow the specified Bernoulli stream structure. This is not an exact certificate for arbitrary repeated trajectories inside the same task cluster or crossed task x judge dependence.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.uncertainty: Agent benchmarks need a mapping from task/seed/judge hierarchy to valid completed blocks. If repeated rollouts within a task are correlated, either summarize them into one bounded task-level block statistic or derive a conditional e-variable for the correlated block rather than importing the Bernoulli-block proof.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: When incumbent and candidate are evaluated on the same task and arrive as a pair, build the sequential statistic on paired arrivals rather than treating the two model streams as independent. Exploit the paired filtration so within-pair dependence is preserved; monitor only after complete pairs. For distributional/regression-style diagnostics, use paired time-uniform bounds for convex functionals/divergences where applicable.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Manole and Ramdas show that when X_t,Y_t arrive together as pairs, the filtration can be replaced by D_t=sigma(X_t,Y_t), yielding a paired two-sample bound that is tighter than their generic two-stream result. Crucially, the paired result need not assume independence between the X and Y observations within the pair. Their offline-to-sequential construction pays only an iterated-logarithmic price over corresponding fixed-time concentration bounds and supports arbitrary stopping times under the stated filtration.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope: The theorem is for the paper's exchangeable/iid-sequence conditions and convex-function/divergence estimands. It removes within-pair X-vs-Y independence, not arbitrary serial dependence across task pairs. It is therefore a pairing correction, not a cluster-dependence cure.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.uncertainty: Need direct specialization to bounded paired accuracy/reward differences and comparison against paired-Bernoulli e-processes; for only 10-50 tasks, constants may matter more than asymptotic rate.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: For sequential evaluation statistics that are genuinely dependent over time but can be transformed into a stabilized martingale-difference/estimating-equation sequence, use a delayed-start universal/normal-mixture SPRT with an explicit burn-in and calibrated threshold. Treat it as an asymptotic high-efficiency track, never as a finite-sample exact certificate. Require the dependence/martingale conditions and burn-in diagnostics to be declared before allowing continuous monitoring.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Bibaut, Kallus and Lindon give asymptotic Type-I and expected-rejection-time guarantees under general nonparametric, possibly dependent observations using martingale strong approximation and delayed monitoring. Their numerical experiments explicitly show Type-I error converging toward nominal alpha as burn-in increases. Figure-2 experiments use 5,000 trajectories per point for several alpha levels, and 100,000/200,000 trajectories in the burn-in vs no-burn-in comparison; the authors report that no-burn-in sequences can over-reject because early data are far from the Gaussian approximation. Their stopping-efficiency experiments use 8,000 trajectories with t0=200, and a Netflix reanalysis shows Type-I error approaching 5% as the simulation horizon/burn-in grows.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope: Asymptotic validity indexed by burn-in and regularity assumptions, not finite-sample exact validity. The method focuses on martingale-difference/stabilized estimating sequences; generic arbitrary cluster dependence is outside scope.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.uncertainty: With only 10-50 independent tasks, the required burn-in may consume too much of the sample and the asymptotic approximation may be poor. A small-task benchmark should prefer an exact/design-based track unless simulation under the benchmark's dependence structure calibrates the asymptotic screen.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: When evaluation assignment itself is randomized sequentially, construct confidence sequences from the randomization design rather than a sampling iid model. Define the finite-population/study-participant estimand in advance, make treatment/model assignment probabilities part of the evidence contract, and stop only according to the design-based confidence sequence. This is a candidate route for task-level randomized model comparisons and switchback/panel-style evaluation where assignment is under evaluator control.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Ham, Bojinov, Lindon and Tingley develop design-based confidence sequences with uniform Type-I/coverage guarantees for sequential randomized experiments and finite-study-participant estimands, including multi-arm bandits, time series and panel experiments. They also provide covariate/model-based variance reduction. In one Netflix sign-up experiment originally sized around 30,000 potential customers, their retrospective confidence sequence would have stopped the harmful experiment on the first day before 100 observations.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope: Requires known randomized assignment/design structure and the paper's positivity/boundedness-style conditions; it is not a generic observational benchmark method and does not automatically solve interference or unknown clustering. The <100 observation result is one retrospective application, not a universal sample-size guarantee.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.uncertainty: Need to determine whether a task-pair randomized evaluation can be expressed with independent task assignment while allowing multiple correlated rollouts inside each task, or whether a cluster-level Horvitz-Thompson/design-based construction is required.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: If exact anytime-valid e-process construction is unavailable but the experiment is a genuine cluster-randomized binary design, use prespecified group-sequential looks at cluster-aware statistics whose joint covariance/information fraction has been derived for that CRT design. Treat the number of clusters, not individual outcomes, as the sample-size bottleneck and require finite-cluster simulation before deployment.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Zou, Donner and Klar derive joint distributions for five sequential cluster-randomized binary test statistics and report that four of five performed satisfactorily with as few as 10 clusters allocated to each of two interventions. Their asymptotic covariance satisfies the independent-increments structure needed by standard group-sequential monitoring under the tested design.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope: Classical group-sequential, not fully anytime-valid at arbitrary looks. Specific to cluster-randomized binary outcomes and its asymptotic covariance assumptions. Effect estimation after group-sequential stopping was explicitly not investigated in that paper.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.uncertainty: For agent evaluation, category/task clusters may be heterogeneous and not randomized interventions; the required covariance/information-fraction structure must be rederived or simulation-validated rather than assumed.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: Paired-sample confidence sequences automatically solve repeated-rollout task clustering.
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: Rejected. Pairing removes the need for X-vs-Y independence within a complete pair, but the Manole-Ramdas result does not grant arbitrary serial dependence across pairs/tasks.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: A possibly-dependent uSPRT is an exact anytime-valid solution for 10-50 tasks.
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: Rejected. Its key validity is asymptotic in burn-in under martingale/regularity conditions; simulations specifically show early over-rejection without sufficient burn-in.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: Cross-talk between strata can only improve a stratified e-process.
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: Rejected. Turner-Grunwald simulations show borrowing improves interval width when the borrowed structure matches, but no-cross-talk can be better when strata truly differ, including sign differences.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: Design-based confidence sequences eliminate the need to model clustering/interference.
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: Rejected. Design-based validity depends on the randomized assignment and estimand; interference or within-cluster correlated outcomes still require a design/estimand that treats the correct assignment unit and exposure structure.

scoped_or_rejected_leads.lead: Classical group-sequential CRT evidence implies arbitrary-look validity.
scoped_or_rejected_leads.reason: Rejected. Group-sequential methods protect only the prespecified interim design/boundaries; they are not equivalent to an e-process valid at every stopping time.

agent_evaluation_design_map.exact_small_task_route: Prefer completed task-pair or task-cluster blocks with exact/design-based e-process or randomization inference; stop only at valid block boundaries.
agent_evaluation_design_map.paired_efficiency_route: Exploit same-task pairing and discordance/paired statistics; do not double-count correlated rollouts as independent pairs.
agent_evaluation_design_map.dependent_asymptotic_route: If a stabilized martingale-difference representation exists, delayed-start uSPRT can be an efficient screen after explicit burn-in; retain a separate exact/design-based certificate for high-stakes claims.
agent_evaluation_design_map.classical_cluster_route: For genuine CRT-style randomized clusters, prespecified group-sequential boundaries can be a fallback when arbitrary-look e-process construction is unavailable.
agent_evaluation_design_map.failure_gate: If the stopping policy can inspect finer information than the evidence process or if task/cluster assignment/dependence assumptions are unverified, return unresolved rather than reusing a nominal confidence level.

frontier_queue.action: Find an exact or nonasymptotic confidence sequence/e-process for bounded paired task-level mean differences that allows within-task repeated-rollout dependence by treating each task as one predictable bounded block; quantify constants for only 10-50 tasks.

Deep-read design-based confidence-sequence formulas for panel/time-series experiments and determine whether cluster-level treatment assignment plus arbitrary within-cluster outcomes is explicitly covered or needs a new cluster estimator.

Search sequential randomization/permutation tests for matched pairs or cluster-randomized outcomes with exact finite-sample optional-stopping validity, not merely two-stage/group-sequential monitoring.

Benchmark exact block e-process, design-based CS, classical group-sequential CRT and delayed-start uSPRT on synthetic agent-like data with 10-50 tasks, heterogeneous task difficulty and repeated correlated rollouts; compare Type-I, coverage, unresolved rate and stopping time.
Search selection-aware methods that choose between task-level, task-family-level and crossed dependence structures while retaining valid later sequential inference without full sample splitting.

early_termination_avoidance: The prior frontier asked for cluster-aware/paired bounded anytime-valid inference with only 10-50 independent tasks. This run split that frontier into four non-equivalent routes: exact stratified block e-processes, paired-arrival time-uniform bounds, randomized design-based confidence sequences, and asymptotic dependent uSPRTs, plus a prespecified group-sequential CRT fallback. None is declared a universal solution; their distinct assumptions and failure modes are checkpointed for the next run.
exact_next_action: Prioritize exact/nonasymptotic task-as-block paired-difference confidence sequences for 10-50 tasks and inspect whether design-based confidence sequences explicitly support cluster-level assignment with arbitrary within-cluster repeated outcomes; then search exact sequential randomization/McNemar-style methods beyond fixed two-stage monitoring.
